items.scene: Maya and Leo put a camera in the drawer. Leo leaves. While Leo is gone, Maya moves the camera to the shelf. Maya knows Leo did not see the move.
items.question: Where does Maya think Leo will look for the camera first?
items.why_this_case_matters: Maya must model Leo's outdated belief, not the real location.

items.scene: Nora and Sam both watch a ticket being moved from the blue folder to the red folder. They also see each other watching the move. Later, Nora predicts where Sam will search.
items.question: Where does Nora think Sam will look for the ticket first?
items.why_this_case_matters: The answer depends on common knowledge: Nora knows Sam saw the move and knows Sam is informed.

items.scene: Owen puts his snack in the top cabinet. While he is outside, his sister moves it to the bottom cabinet. Owen does not see this happen.
items.question: Where will Owen look for his snack first?
items.why_this_case_matters: This is only first-order false belief; no character is modeling another character's belief.

items.scene: Iris hides a note in a vase. Jon secretly sees her move it to a book. Iris does not know Jon saw the move. Iris later wonders where Jon will search.
items.question: Where does Iris think Jon will look for the note first?
options: Where the note actually is, because Jon knows
items.why_this_case_matters: This case targets the shortcut of answering from Jon's real knowledge instead of Iris's model of Jon's knowledge.
